title: Development of a <sup>18</sup>F-labeled PET radioligand for imaging 5-HT<sub>1B</sub> receptors: [<sup>18</sup>F]AZ10419096.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: In the last decade PET has been useful in studying and understanding the 5-HT<sub>1B</sub> receptor. [<sup>11</sup>C]AZ10419369 and [<sup>11</sup>C]P943 have been applied as radioligands in these studies. Both use carbon-11 (t<sub>1/2</sub> = 20.4 min) as radionuclide, which limits the application to PET centres that have an on-site cyclotron and radiochemistry facilities. In this paper we report the synthesis and initial evaluation of the first fluorine-18 PET radioligand to image 5-HT<sub>1B</sub> receptors in brain, [<sup>18</sup>F]AZ10419096. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A boronate-precursor for [<sup>18</sup>F]AZ10419096 was synthesized from an intermediate provided by AstraZeneca and was labeled with fluorine 18 using Cu-mediated radio-fluorination. [<sup>18</sup>F]AZ10419096 was used in PET baseline and pretreatment measurements in nonhuman primates. PET data were analyzed using SRTM using the cerebellum as reference region. Blood samples for radio-metabolite analysis were collected during PET measurements. RESULTS: Radio-fluorination gave [<sup>18</sup>F]AZ10419096 in sufficient amounts and molar activity and with high radiochemical purity to be applied in PET measurements. In a baseline PET measurement [<sup>18</sup>F]AZ10419096 showed a high brain uptake and regional distribution consistent with reported 5-HT<sub>1B</sub> receptor densities. In a pretreatment PET measurement, AR-A000002 (2.0 mg/kg) blocked the binding of [<sup>18</sup>F]AZ10419096 to 5-HT<sub>1B</sub> receptors in occipital cortex by 80%, thereby demonstrating high specific binding. CONCLUSION: [<sup>18</sup>F]AZ10419096 is the first fluorine-18 PET radioligand for imaging 5-HT<sub>1B</sub> receptors in vivo with high specific binding and binding potential. [<sup>18</sup>F]AZ10419096 is a candidate for further development for use in clinical PET studies.
